Before you remix, please make sure that you followed all the rules:

Only @BarryFans, @ZYellow, @Burgnew_On_A_Laptop, @Twin138956Scratch, @Kyle3912Again, @Eliminated, and @ScratchTeen9300 (as well as their other accounts) are allowed to break these rules.
Rules marked with a (!) can only be broken by @BarryFans, nobody else!

(!) 1. Remember REMIX ETIQUETTE: Comment "Remixing..." in the comments before starting a remix, so people know not to accidentally split the remix tree's branches. If you don't intend to make a new remix branch, then don't remix if someone has commented "Remixing...".
(!) 2. DO NOT BREAK SCRATCH'S COMMUNITY GUIDELINES!! That means nothing too scary or vulgar & no swear words!
(!) 3. Don't add or remove anyone from the breaking rules list without permission! Furthermore, don't delete any of these rules or instructions & don't completely change the project title either!
4. Don't delete or destructively modify anything you didn't make! You are allowed to do this though if something breaks any rules or the Community Guidelines or if you need to fix a bug or glitch.
5. Don't make your characters too large, that would make it hard to see. I would suggest scaling your character IN THE COSTUME EDITOR to match the size of the other characters before making your other costumes.
(!) 6. (PLEASE respect ZYellow's opinion on this) Please DON'T add any content from FNF, that means no characters, references, AND music tracks from that game. The reason why this rule exists is because FNF was involved in an incident with the New Oddball Mirror Hall. That incident caused problems for ZYellow much later and it tarnished his opinion on that game (if you like that game, then ZYellow respects your opinion).
7. Please refrain from adding any static images for characters, even if you attempt animate them, background included or not (EG: A PNG or JPEG of a Minecraft mob or some other thing).
8. I don't recommend adding any singular characters that appear to be 2 separate characters (EG: Mario & Luigi both as 1 character), unless they are stuck together with no feasible way to physically detach them OR if one of them appears in a stunned costume of the other.
9. Don't delete any music tracks unless they break the Community Guidelines. If you don't want to listen to a certain song or genre, utilize the "audio exemption" functionality to make sure you can't.
10. On the topic of music, please also refer to the Music comment's recommended music limit so that it can't have too much lag from this project.
11. You can add yourself to the thumbnail, but please don't delete any characters off it or completely change it altogether! I also recommend that you group your characters to prevent clutter.

--- HOW 2 REMIX ---
Want to add a character to this game? Follow these instructions carefully to get them in:
1. Scroll down below these instructions & read the rules! DON'T proceed until you've done this!
2. Click the green "Remix" button at the top-right corner (duh)
3. Create a duplicate of the "Player0" sprite, and follow the instructions I put in.
4. Create your character! Replace every costume in the duplicated sprite EXCEPT for the "Edge-Breaker" and "SizeBox" costumes with your character, replace all "Voice" sound clips with your character's voice & set their name.
5. Test your project &, if you like the result, either continue to add more characters or share it!
BONUS: You're also allowed to add characters to the thumbnail & add more music tracks.
6. Before you share your project, PLEASE make sure that you credit @-Rex- for the Pen Text Engine++!
If you don't want to type their username, here's a template that you can copy and paste:

Credit to @-Rex- for Pen Text Engine++ ( https://scratch.mit.edu/projects/406678232/ ).

⚠ WARNING: Do NOT delete this sprite! This is used for adding a player into the game. To get started, copy this sprite, then follow the instructions I put in.

Set your character's name, seconds per frame, how many delight, dismay, and "ouch" voices they have, and their player number here. I recommend you don't make your characters too big or too small, otherwise it would make it too hard to see.

⚠ WARNING: If you do not change the "Name Here" to your character's name, they will not participate in the game! Also, if you use a name taken by another player (For example: Josh but the name Josh is taken), it would cause unexpected behavior and your remix would become UNOFFICIAL. To get around this, put parentheses after the name and then insert your initials, like this: "Josh (BF)". (BF is short for BarryFans)

If you don't want any seconds per frame, there is a custom block after the player number block that allows you to choose if you want to have seconds per walk frame or not, so you will have to reply with nothing or anything else to have no seconds per frame. 
If you answer Y, your character will have seconds per frame. Otherwise, anything else will not have any seconds per frame.

A2:[.jz)t(dIBXTg@.Fv.text:
Hey there! If you want to add your own music, first separate your song into it's intro (if it has an intro) and it's looping part in separate sounds, tag "-Start" at the end of the intro's name, then tag "-Loop" at the end of the looping part's name. (Jingles won't have these tags, as they aren't intended to loop.) Add the song's name into either "Add music" block, depending on what scenario it should be for, & finally drop it here! Remember that EVERYTHING must be correct spelling or else it won't work! Running a test recommended!

If the music track or jingle comes from a party game, like Mario Party, Wii Party or WarioWare: MEGA Party Game$, make sure it won't play for users who don't want those music tracks, like SmashBrosFan2020, via the audio-exemption lists & Boolean. Same goes for "gets faster" tracks, music from Flash/HTML5 games, lyrical music, non-looping music, and music from Miitopia. I also recommend you please don't add any more than around 100 music tracks and jingles total, to prevent lag or the dreaded "refusal-to-save glitch" when modifying the project on less powerful devices. It's also best to refrain from adding too many music tracks longer than 3 minutes (180 seconds) or too many "gets faster" tracks.
